text:
Looking at the diff, the line

```javascript
var decimalPlaces = (options && options.decimalPlaces !== undefined) ? options.decimalPlaces : 2;
```

was replaced with

```javascript
var decimalPlaces = (options && true) ? options.decimalPlaces : 2;
```

This breaks the default-decimals fallback. Previously, when an options object was supplied *without* `decimalPlaces`, the code fell back to `2`. Now, whenever `options` is truthy, `options.decimalPlaces` is used directly — which is `undefined` in that case. `Number.prototype.toFixed(undefined)` behaves like `toFixed(0)`, so every `format()` call that passes an options object without `decimalPlaces` silently rounds to zero decimal places.

Examples of the observable difference:
- `bytes(1536, {})` — was `'1.5KB'`, now `'2KB'`
- `bytes(1024, { fixedDecimals: true })` — was `'1.00KB'`, now `'1KB'`
- `bytes(1536, { thousandsSeparator: ',' })` — was `'1.5KB'`, now `'2KB'`

Calls with no options at all still work (because `options && true` is falsy when `options` is undefined), which is why the library's own test suite can stay green while this regresses. The test below passes on 3.1.2 and fails on the patched build.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "test/proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar bytes = require('..');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('fails on the patched build', function () {\n    // options without decimalPlaces must still default to 2 decimal places\n    assert.strictEqual(bytes(1536, {}), '1.5KB');\n    assert.strictEqual(bytes(1024, { fixedDecimals: true }), '1.00KB');\n    assert.strictEqual(bytes.format(1536, { thousandsSeparator: ',' }), '1.5KB');\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The guard `options && options.decimalPlaces !== undefined` was weakened to `options && true`, so when options are given without decimalPlaces, `undefined` reaches toFixed() (treated as 0) instead of the default of 2. Any format() call with an options object lacking decimalPlaces now rounds to whole units, e.g. bytes(1536, {}) returns '2KB' instead of '1.5KB'."}
```
